title: Channel Coding Converse via Fano's Inequality
description: Proves the asymptotic channel coding converse: when transmission rate R exceeds channel capacity C, the error probability is bounded away from zero for sufficiently long codes. For block length n ≥ 2/(R-C), any code with rate ≥ R has error probability ≥ (R-C)/(2R) > 0. The proof combines Fano's inequality and the memoryless channel mutual information bound into a single axiom, then derives the quantitative lower bound on error probability via algebraic manipulation.

overview.historicalContext:
Claude Shannon's 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' introduced both the channel coding theorem (achievability) and its converse in a single landmark paper. The converse — that no code can achieve reliable communication above capacity — is arguably the more fundamental result: it establishes capacity C as a hard upper limit, not merely an achievable benchmark. Shannon's original proof of the converse used a combinatorial counting argument; the modern form using Fano's inequality became standard through the work of Feinstein (1954) and Wolf/Fano in the 1950s.

Robert Fano (1952) proved the inequality that bears his name: for any random variables W (input) and Ŵ (estimate), H(W|Ŵ) ≤ H_b(P_e) + P_e·log(M-1), where H_b is the binary entropy. Combined with Shannon's chain rule H(W) = I(W;Y^n) + H(W|Y^n), this yields a clean algebraic bound. The 'strong converse' — that P_e → 1 as n → ∞ for any rate R > C, not just P_e bounded away from 0 — was proved by Wolfowitz (1957) and requires a more refined argument. This formalization proves the weaker (but classical) asymptotic converse, with an explicit quantitative threshold N = ⌈2/(R-C)⌉.
overview.problemStatement:
**Channel Coding Converse (Asymptotic)**:
For any discrete memoryless channel with capacity $C$ and any rate $R > C$, there exists $\delta > 0$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $n \geq N$, any block code of length $n$ with rate $\geq R$ satisfies:
$$P_e \geq \delta = \frac{R-C}{2R} > 0$$
Specifically, $N = \lceil 2/(R-C) \rceil$ suffices.
overview.text: Proves the asymptotic channel coding converse: error probability is bounded away from zero at rates above capacity.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof has four stages:

1. **Combined bound (axiom)**: fano_mi_converse_bound axiomatizes the three information-theoretic steps that together give log M ≤ n·C + 1 + P_e·log M. The three steps are: (i) H(W) = log M for uniform sources, (ii) I(W;Y^n) ≤ n·C by memoryless channel MI chain rule, (iii) H(W|Ŵ) ≤ 1 + P_e·log M by Fano's inequality with h(P_e) ≤ log 2 ≤ 1 nat.

2. **Algebraic bound (converse_from_combined_bound)**: From log M ≤ n·C + 1 + P_e·log M and log M ≥ n·R, derive P_e ≥ 1 - (n·C+1)/(n·R). The main step is (1-P_e)·log M ≤ n·C+1, combined with log M ≥ n·R to get (1-P_e)·n·R ≤ n·C+1.

3. **Threshold bound (threshold_bound)**: Show that for n ≥ 2/(R-C), we have (R-C)/(2R) ≤ 1 - (n·C+1)/(n·R). The key algebraic fact is n·(R-C) ≥ 2 implies n·R² ≥ n·C·R + 2R, which gives the bound after clearing denominators.

4. **Main theorem**: Combine steps 2 and 3 to get P_e ≥ (R-C)/(2R) for all n ≥ ⌈2/(R-C)⌉.
keyInsights: Fano's inequality converts the error probability condition into a conditional entropy bound, enabling the algebraic chain
The memoryless assumption on the channel is essential: it allows I(W;Y^n) ≤ n·C via the MI chain rule for product channels
The asymptotic threshold n ≥ 2/(R-C) is tight up to constants: as n → ∞, the bound approaches P_e ≥ 1 - C/R
The gap δ = (R-C)/(2R) is a quantitative lower bound; the true P_e → 1 - C/R as n → ∞ by the strong converse
The proof establishes existence of N via ⌈2/(R-C)⌉, giving an explicit threshold rather than just ∃N

sections.title: Combined Fano-MI Converse Bound (Axiom)
sections.description: Axiomatizes the three-step information-theoretic argument: H(W)=log M, I(W;Y^n)≤n·C, H(W|Ŵ)≤1+P_e·log M. Together these give log M ≤ n·C + 1 + P_e·log M.
sections.summary: Key axiom combining Fano inequality and memoryless channel MI bound.

sections.title: Algebraic Converse Lemma
sections.description: From the Fano-MI bound and the rate condition log M ≥ n·R, derives P_e ≥ 1 - (n·C+1)/(n·R) by algebraic manipulation.
sections.summary: Derives the P_e lower bound from the combined Fano-MI inequality.
sections.mathContext: $\log M \geq nR,\; \log M \leq nC+1+P_e\log M \implies P_e \geq 1 - \frac{nC+1}{nR}$

sections.title: Threshold Lemma
sections.description: For n ≥ 2/(R-C), proves (R-C)/(2R) ≤ 1 - (n·C+1)/(n·R) by clearing denominators and using the key polynomial inequality n·R² ≥ n·C·R + 2R.
sections.summary: Shows the gap (R-C)/(2R) appears once n exceeds the threshold 2/(R-C).

sections.title: Gap Positivity
sections.description: The gap δ = (R-C)/(2R) is strictly positive when R > C.
sections.summary: δ > 0 whenever the rate exceeds capacity.

sections.title: Rate-Log Lemma
sections.description: Translates the rate condition R ≤ rate_of_code into the log form n·R ≤ log M needed for the main proof.
sections.summary: Converts rate ≥ R into the log M ≥ n·R inequality.

sections.title: Channel Coding Converse (Asymptotic)
sections.description: The main theorem: for R > C, the gap δ = (R-C)/(2R) is positive and any code with rate ≥ R and block length n ≥ ⌈2/(R-C)⌉ has error probability ≥ δ.
sections.summary: Main result: P_e ≥ (R-C)/(2R) for sufficiently long codes at rates above capacity.

conclusion.summary: This formalization proves the asymptotic channel coding converse: at rates above capacity, error probability is bounded away from zero for sufficiently long codes. The proof introduces one axiom (fano_mi_converse_bound) capturing three information-theoretic steps that require probability-theoretic formalism not yet in Lean's Mathlib. All algebraic manipulation from the bound to the quantitative P_e ≥ (R-C)/(2R) lower bound is fully proved in Lean with no sorries.
conclusion.implications: Together with the achievability direction (channel_coding_achievability axiom in ShannonChannelCoding.lean), this establishes capacity C as the sharp threshold: reliable communication is possible below C and impossible above C. The quantitative bound P_e ≥ (R-C)/(2R) gives an explicit rate of degradation as R → C from above.
